explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The family heads say the LORD commanded Moses "to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters." (Numbers 36:2) They aren't arguing with the ruling here. They're starting from it, like a baker who reads the recipe card out loud before asking one question about the oven.

I see why you'd go there, friend. Brothers are the family heads speaking, and they call Zelophehad "our brother." But the verse says the LORD commanded that his inheritance go to his daughters (Numbers 36:2). The men are reminding Moses of the ruling, not asking for the land.

Nephews would make sense in plenty of families, friend. But the family heads say the LORD commanded Moses to give Zelophehad's inheritance to his daughters (Numbers 36:2). No nephews are mentioned in this verse at all.

explanations.answer: It is added to the tribe they marry into
explanations.explanation: Right on the money, baker. The family heads say that if the daughters marry men from other tribes, their inheritance "will be withdrawn from the portion of our fathers and added to the tribe into which they marry." (Numbers 36:3) Their worry is that their own allotted inheritance would be taken away. It's like a batch of cookies leaving your counter and ending up on the neighbor's.

explanations.answer: It goes back to Moses to give out again
explanations.explanation: Nice thinking, but Moses isn't the one who ends up with it. The family heads say the land would be "added to the tribe into which they marry." (Numbers 36:3) Nothing in the verse sends it back to Moses to give out again.

explanations.answer: It is split up among the tribe of Levi
explanations.explanation: Good guess, friend, but Levi never comes up in this verse. The family heads say the land would be withdrawn from their fathers' portion and "added to the tribe into which they marry." (Numbers 36:3) That's the tribe of the husband, whichever one it is.

That's the one, baker. Moses says, "The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaks correctly." (Numbers 36:5) And he says it at the word of the LORD, so it's not just Moses giving his opinion. These men raised a concern, and it was heard.

I get it, friend, since the land was given out by lot (Numbers 36:2). But Moses never tells them to trust the lot. He says, "The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaks correctly." (Numbers 36:5) They aren't brushed off at all.

Oh, that would be a cold answer, friend, and Moses doesn't give it. He says, "The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaks correctly." (Numbers 36:5) He says it at the word of the LORD. Their concern was heard, not scolded.

explanations.answer: Anyone in a clan of their father's tribe
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. The command says, "They may marry anyone they please, provided they marry within a clan of the tribe of their father." (Numbers 36:6) So they get real freedom to choose, with one limit on the tribe. Plenty of room, and just one rule.

explanations.answer: Only men Moses picks for them
explanations.explanation: I can see how a big rule sounds like that, friend. But the command starts with "They may marry anyone they please." (Numbers 36:6) Moses isn't handing out husbands. The only condition is a clan of their father's tribe.

explanations.answer: Any man from any tribe of Israel
explanations.explanation: Close, but that's the very thing the family heads were worried about. The command says they may marry anyone they please, "provided they marry within a clan of the tribe of their father." (Numbers 36:6) So the choice is wide, but it stays inside their father's tribe.

explanations.answer: Each Israelite keeps his fathers' tribal land
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Moses says it's because "each of the Israelites is to retain the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers." (Numbers 36:7) The land is meant to stay in the family line it was given to. That's the whole reason, and the text states it plainly.

explanations.answer: The tribes would start fighting over borders
explanations.explanation: That sounds like something real, friend, but Moses never says it. The reason he gives is that "each of the Israelites is to retain the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers." (Numbers 36:7) Nothing about fighting or borders appears in the verse.

explanations.answer: The lots can never be cast a second time
explanations.explanation: Good try, since the land was given by lot (Numbers 36:2). But Moses doesn't say anything about casting lots again here. His reason is that "each of the Israelites is to retain the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers." (Numbers 36:7)

I see why it looks that way, baker, since this all started with Zelophehad's daughters. But Moses widens it: "Every daughter who possesses an inheritance from any Israelite tribe must marry within a clan of the tribe of her father." (Numbers 36:8) So the rule isn't just for those five sisters. It covers every daughter in Israel who inherits.

That's right, friend. Moses says, "Every daughter who possesses an inheritance from any Israelite tribe must marry within a clan of the tribe of her father." (Numbers 36:8) So it isn't only for Zelophehad's daughters. It covers every daughter in Israel who holds an inheritance.

explanations.answer: They obey and do as they were told
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The text says, "So the daughters of Zelophehad did as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 36:10) No arguing and no stalling in the verse. They simply did it.

explanations.answer: They ask Moses to change the ruling
explanations.explanation: That's a reasonable thought, friend, but it's not what happens. The text says the daughters "did as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 36:10) Nothing is said about them asking for a change.

explanations.answer: They give the land to their uncles
explanations.explanation: Interesting idea, friend, but it's not in the text. The daughters "did as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 36:10) That command was about who they could marry, and their land stays with them.
Right, baker. The text says the five sisters "were married to cousins on their father's side." (Numbers 36:11) That's how they stayed within their father's tribe. The marrying part was handled.

I can see the guess, friend, but servants aren't in this verse. It says the daughters "were married to cousins on their father's side." (Numbers 36:11) Their husbands came from their father's own family.

Neighbors would be nice, friend, but that's not what the text says. The daughters "were married to cousins on their father's side." (Numbers 36:11) The husbands were family, not just folks living nearby.

That's right, baker. The text says they "married within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained within the tribe of their father's clan." (Numbers 36:12) The command was followed, and the land stayed where it belonged. Everything lined up.

I get why you'd be careful, friend, but this one is true. The text says the daughters married within the clans of Manasseh, "and their inheritance remained within the tribe of their father's clan." (Numbers 36:12) The land didn't move to another tribe.
